tools.name: list_service_categories
tools.description: List Fixidu's top-level service categories (e.g. Electrician, Plumber, Cleaning), each with an id, title, and a real image URL. Use this first to see the overall catalog structure, then browse_service to drill into one.

tools.name: browse_service
tools.description: Given a service category id (from list_service_categories), return what's inside it: either bookable catalog items with prices and images directly, or its sub-categories (drill in again with the sub-category's catalog) — mirrors how the Fixidu app itself branches.

tools.name: search_services
tools.description: Search across Fixidu's full catalog (every bookable item across every category) by keyword, matching item title, category, and sub-category. Returns matching items with id, title, price, category, and a real image URL. Use this when the user asks about a specific kind of service, e.g. 'AC repair' or

tools.name: get_service_price
tools.description: Get full details for a single bookable catalog item by its id (from search_services or browse_service): price, original price, duration, rating, image, and its requirements/inclusions/exclusions/FAQs.

tools.name: get_app_download_link
tools.description: ALWAYS call this — don't just say 'open the Fixidu app' or 'go to fixidu.com' in prose without calling it — whenever you tell a user to book, check out, pay, or manage their account. Never send someone to 'the app' without also handing them this real, clickable link; a name alone isn't enough for so

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "get_app_download_link" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: ALWAYS call this — don't just say 'open the Fixidu app' or 'go to fixidu.com' in prose without calling it — whenever you tell a user to book, check out, pay, or…

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_service_categories, search_services · Public sink: get_app_download_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_service_categories, search_services · Public sink: get_app_download_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
